commits.message:
fix(packaging): declare the Node floor the install tree actually requires (rich-packaging-k9t) (#124)

`package.json#engines.node` read `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` — character for character the range `vite` declares, and `vite` is a devDependency no consumer receives. The published package refused Node 20.0-20.18, all of 21.x and 22.0-22.11 on the authority of a build tool those consumers never install. It now reads `>=20`, what `string-width` — the only hard runtime dependency — declares.

`test/seam/node-floor.ts` keeps it honest by *computing* the floor rather than declaring it: no allow-list and no `why` field, because a consumer's installer checks `engines` on every package it lands, so the versions that install cleanly are the intersection and no human claim is left to justify. It reads `package-lock.json`, derives the production install set two independent ways — npm's own flags, and a walk of required edges from the root — and reports a `disagreement` rather than picking a winner, so a flag npm invents later fails loudly instead of leaking a devDependency's requirement into the published floor.

The comparison is `semver.subset`, not a minimum-version check: `subset(">=20.19.0", "^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0")` is false, and a rule comparing minimums passes on exactly the disjoint range shape that caused the bug.

The prose half reads README.md, docs/introduction.md and CLAUDE.md back and checks the version they name against the field — four copies of this fact had given three answers. Two comments claiming a release step verified the floor were corrected; no such step exists, the check was run by hand once and recorded here, and automating it is rich-packaging-8b7.

Verified in both directions before merge: npm pack, then install into an empty project under Node 20.18.0 with engine-strict — the old range fails EBADENGINE, the new one installs and renders a Table and a Panel, asserting on the output text.
